previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, hematuria, and left flank pain, consistent with pyelonephritis in the setting of a chronic indwelling Foley catheter and recurrent UTIs. He was treated with IV ceftriaxone initially, then transitioned to IM ertapenem due to the emergence of Augmentin-resistant E. coli and concerns about oral adherence given his history of substance use. His infection resolved, and he was afebrile for 48 hours prior to discharge. Acute kidney injury improved with IV fluids, and creatinine decreased from 3.4 to 2.6. Pain management continued with observed dosing of oxycodone and Percocet. He was discharged home with a visiting nurse to administer daily ertapenem injections and instructions to follow up with primary care and urology.
